harness.what: scratch harness (not committed): the CPU-time instrument of #97, the native scene main_native.tscn, headless, one Godot process per run; it plays the four windows of the protocol through the GameServices node the way tests/frontier-comparison-scenario.gd does

windows.ai-phase: from the frame that accepts End Turn to the frame before the one that delivers turn_ended; two scenarios: soak (no selection) and soak-city (the city screen open, the heaviest context); 2 warm-up + 60 measured turns each
windows.event-burst: from the frame that delivers turn_ended to the first frame, at least five from the start, after which stats().events equals notifications_emitted() (B: the same frame, so five frames); same turns
windows.context-switches: the 12-switch round of tests/frontier-comparison-cycle.gd (a new game each round, with its setups), 24 warm-up + 200 measured occurrences of 3 frames (the protocol has 50 measured; more here for a steadier p95)
windows.stress: stress_begin in a frame, 20 stress_step one per frame, two frames after the last: 23 frames; 2 warm-up + 30 measured rounds; stress_end outside the window

harness.quantity: the protocol outcome per window: p95 of the CPU time per frame over the measured occurrences of a run, then the median over the runs; p50, p99, mean and the sum of the frames of an occurrence are kept beside it
harness.headless: no draw: setup and render terms are 0, so the time is the script and the layout of the frame; a windowed run was not made (windowed lanes of other slots were in use)
harness.calibration: the machine was shared with other work (1-minute load average between 4 and 10) and ran in slower states, so a fixed piece of GDScript on data of its own was timed (best of 5) between the phases of every run; the normalized figures divide each phase by the mean of the two calibrations around it over 82 us, the speed of the fastest state seen
harness.notComparative: outside any comparative execution: the protocol load limit (2.0) was not met and these numbers are not entered in any statistic
